record.what_it_does: Customer service platform that unifies customer conversations across channels around people, not tickets.
record.auth_notes: HTTP Basic auth using the agent email and an API token. Tokens are created per agent under More settings > API Tokens, and the user needs the API User permission. The page says a token can perform any API request without restriction. No OAuth is mentioned. The Public Answers API needs no token.
record.access_notes: Tokens come from inside a customer's Gladly organization, and an admin must grant the API User permission. Gladly is enterprise software with no public self-serve signup. I did not fetch a pricing page. A separate sandbox exists at {organization}.gladly.qa, but it is presumably also provisioned through Gladly.
record.api_breadth_notes: Resource groups include Agents, Public Answers, Answer Management, Business Hours, Communications, Conversations, Customers, Export, Inboxes, Reports, Tasks, Teams, Topics and Webhooks, plus a Lookup API. I did not count operations.
record.mcp_notes: No official Gladly MCP server found. Third-party hosted options exist: StackOne (https://www.stackone.com/connectors/gladly/mcp/) and Truto.
record.blocker_notes: The API is broad and well documented, but a developer cannot get credentials alone. Each end user's Gladly admin must issue a per-agent API token, and the token has full, unscoped access. There is no OAuth flow for multi-user apps. Users must paste their organization subdomain, agent email and token.
